Coverage area: All non-AC services of the four state RTCs inside Karnataka, subject to the existing distance limits (KSRTC norm: up to 60 km one-way between residence and institution)..
Who is eligible: Any regular student enrolled in a recognised school, PU college, degree, diploma, ITI, professional, medical, evening or PhD course in Karnataka. Also extended to Karnataka-domicile students studying in neighbouring states and to students from border districts.

Apply free online; Rs 30 service charge at Bangalore One / Karnataka One / Grama One centres. Collect the smart card in person at the designated counter. (https://sevaone.karnataka.gov.in/).
Notes: State Transport Department order effective 12 June 2026. Covers non-AC BMTC and KSRTC ordinary services only; it does NOT cover BMTC AC/Vajra, Vayu Vajra or luxury KSRTC classes. Girl students already travel free under Shakti and do not need this pass. Existing pass holders for 2026-27 are being refunded via Seva Sindhu.

Who is eligible: Women and transgender residents of Karnataka (photo ID / domicile proof).
Documents required: Aadhaar or any Karnataka residence/identity proof; Shakti smart card where already issued.
How and where to apply: No application needed for most travellers — just carry ID. The Shakti smart card is issued through the Seva Sindhu portal. (https://sevasindhu.karnataka.gov.in).

# Who issues what

BMTC issues student passes for travel inside Bengaluru's city network. KSRTC issues
student passes for travel on mofussil (inter-city / inter-town) services, including
the Kanakapura Road corridor that runs through Harohalli. Both corporations use the
same state application portal, Seva Sindhu, and the same broad category structure.

# Student pass categories and the pre-2026 fee structure

Pass fees depend on the course, not on the distance travelled. The published
2025-26 category fees were:

text:
# Student pass categories and the pre-2026 fee structure

These published fees are now largely historical: from 12 June 2026 the state pays
the pass fee for all students on non-AC services (see the free pass document). The
figures remain useful because the *category* you fall into still decides the pass
validity window and the distance limits that apply.

metadata.heading: Student pass categories and the pre-2026 fee structure

text:
# What a student pass actually covers

A student pass covers unlimited travel on the services named on the pass, for the
validity window, between the student's residence and the institution. It is not a
city-wide travel card:

- BMTC student passes cover BMTC services inside the city network, including
  non-AC ordinary buses and metro feeder services.
- KSRTC student passes cover KSRTC ordinary services on the declared route, under
  the existing distance norm of up to 60 km one-way between residence and
  institution.
- Neither pass covers AC Vajra, Vayu Vajra airport services, Airavat, Ambari,
  Rajahamsa or other luxury classes unless the pass is explicitly an AC pass.

metadata.heading: What a student pass actually covers

text:
# Documents required

The standard document set for a student pass application is:

1. The pass application form, downloaded from Seva Sindhu and signed and stamped by
   the institution.
2. A bonafide certificate from the institution, or the current academic year's fee
   receipt, which serves as proof of enrolment.
3. Aadhaar card.
4. A passport-size photograph. For a smart-card pass, a live photograph is captured
   at the counter when the card is printed.
5. A caste certificate with an RD number, for SC/ST applicants.
6. A mobile number registered on Seva Sindhu, for OTP and collection SMS.

# Documents required

Students who live more than 40 km from the institution may be asked for a
declaration that the course is not available at a closer institution. This affects
many Harohalli and Kanakapura Road commuters.

# Where to apply

Applications are submitted online at the Seva Sindhu / e-District portal
(sevaone.karnataka.gov.in). Applying online is free. Students who need help can use
a Bangalore One, Karnataka One or Grama One centre for a service charge of Rs 30.
After approval, an SMS tells the student which counter to collect the smart card
from. The student must collect it in person.

BMTC collection counters include Majestic (Kempegowda Bus Station), Kengeri,
Shantinagar, Hosakote, Electronic City and Anekal. KSRTC notifies its own list of
pass-issuing counters, which for 2026-27 ran to 123 counters across Karnataka.

# Renewal, replacement and route changes

Student passes are issued for an academic year and must be renewed each year
through the same Seva Sindhu process. If a pass card is lost or damaged, or if the
student changes route, BMTC charges a fixed replacement or route-change fee
(historically Rs 100). Renewal requires the same document set plus the previous
pass.

# Common reasons applications are rejected

- The application form is not signed and stamped by the institution.
- The fee receipt belongs to a previous academic year.
- The name or date of birth does not match the Aadhaar record.
- The photograph is not a recent passport-style photograph.
- The selected collection counter does not handle the applicant's category.
- For SC/ST applicants, the caste certificate RD number is missing.

# What changed

On 12 June 2026 the Karnataka Transport Department issued an order making bus
passes free for all students travelling on non-AC services of the four state road
transport corporations: BMTC, KSRTC, NWKRTC and KKRTC. The scheme was announced by
Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar in the first cabinet meeting after taking office and
implemented within days.

The state bears the pass fee, a processing fee of Rs 100 per pass and an accident
relief fund contribution of Rs 50 per pass (Rs 5 per month of accident insurance
cover). The estimated annual cost of the scheme is Rs 286.08 crore, plus about
Rs 15 crore in processing and accident-relief charges.

# Who is eligible

- Any regular student enrolled in a recognised school, PU college, degree college,
  diploma, ITI, professional course, medical course, evening college, postgraduate
  or PhD programme in Karnataka.
- Karnataka-domicile students studying in institutions in neighbouring states.
- Students from districts bordering Karnataka who study at institutions in
  Karnataka.
- Existing eligibility rules still apply: academic requirements, distance limits
  (up to 60 km one-way between residence and institution under KSRTC norms) and
  pass validity periods are unchanged.

# Who is eligible

Girls and transgender students who are Karnataka residents already travel free
under the Shakti scheme and do not need a separate student pass, although they may
still apply if they prefer to hold a card.

# What the free pass does not cover

- BMTC AC services, including Vajra and Vayu Vajra airport buses.
- KSRTC luxury classes: Airavat, Airavat Club Class, Ambari, Ambari Dream Class,
  Rajahamsa, Rajahamsa Executive, Pallakki, Flybus and EV Power Plus.
- Travel on the portion of an interstate route that leaves Karnataka.
- Namma Metro. The metro is run by BMRCL, not by the four RTCs, and is outside this
  scheme.

A student who needs AC travel must still buy the paid BMTC AC student monthly pass,
which cost Rs 1,400 per month as of the January 2025 revision.

metadata.heading: What the free pass does not cover

text:
# How to apply

1. Go to the Seva Sindhu / e-District portal at sevaone.karnataka.gov.in and log in
   with Aadhaar or mobile OTP.
2. Search for the student bus pass service for the current academic year and choose
   the operator (BMTC, KSRTC, NWKRTC or KKRTC).
3. Fill in personal details, institution details, course and the residence-to-
   institution route.
4. Download the application form, get it signed and stamped by the institution, and
   upload it with the current-year fee receipt, photograph, Aadhaar and, for SC/ST
   applicants, the caste certificate with RD number.
5. Select a convenient pass-issuing counter.
6. On approval, an SMS gives the counter address. Collect the smart card in person;
   a live photograph is taken for the card.

# How to apply

Applying online is free. Applications submitted through Bangalore One, Karnataka
One or Grama One centres attract the usual Rs 30 service charge.

# Refunds for passes already bought

Students who had already paid for a 2026-27 pass between 29 May and 9 June 2026 -
19,792 passes were issued in that window - are entitled to a full refund. Refunds
are claimed on Seva Sindhu with Aadhaar-based e-KYC and bank account details, and
KSRTC has said the money is credited within seven days of applying. Students who
already hold a paid pass can continue to use it until the refund is processed.

# Practical implications for a Harohalli commuter

A student commuting from Jayanagar, Banashankari or Kanakapura Road to the DSU
Harohalli campus, which is roughly 35-45 km from most of Bengaluru, is exactly the
profile this scheme is aimed at. Before June 2026 the same trip needed either a
KSRTC student pass (Rs 1,050 for a college student, 10 months) or a BMTC pass plus
a KSRTC extension, plus daily tickets for the gaps. From 2026-27 the non-AC pass
costs the student nothing, so the only paid alternatives worth considering are the
AC passes and the metro.

metadata.heading: Practical implications for a Harohalli commuter

text:
# Verification advice

The scheme is recent and the rules are still settling. Students should confirm the
current syllabus of fees, counter list and eligibility on Seva Sindhu before paying
anything at a counter. Any agent that quotes an exact fee without checking the
portal is guessing.

# Why KSRTC matters for a Harohalli commute

Harohalli sits about 35-45 km south of central Bengaluru on the Kanakapura Road
corridor, outside the core BBMP area. BMTC does run services this far out: route
213-V (Harohalli to Sanjay Gandhi Hospital), 213-VD (Dayananda Sagara MDC to
Banashankari / Anjanapura) and 213-VB (Bannikuppe Circle / Harohalli Industrial
Area) all reach Harohalli in the GTFS feed. But the corridor is also served by
KSRTC ordinary buses running between Bengaluru (Kempegowda Bus Station) and
Kanakapura, and those buses continue south to Malavalli and Mysuru.

metadata.heading: Why KSRTC matters for a Harohalli commute

text:
# KSRTC pass rules

KSRTC issues monthly season tickets between two named places on a daily-commute
basis. The rules that matter:

- Monthly passes are issued for travel along with a KSRTC photo-identity card,
  which costs Rs 50 and is valid for one year.
- A pass issued for Express services is valid on both Express and Ordinary
  services. A pass issued for Ordinary services is valid only on Ordinary services.
- Season tickets are personal and not transferable.
- Student concessional passes are the cheapest option where they apply, and since
  2026-27 they are free for non-AC services under the state scheme.

# KSRTC pass rules

KSRTC does not publish a single statewide fare table for season tickets. Each
depot prices a pass by the corridor and the number of fare stages. The agent must
never invent a KSRTC monthly pass price; it should quote the corridor and send the
student to the depot.

# Published KSRTC fares on the corridor

Karnataka raised all RTC fares by 15 per cent with effect from 5 January 2025. The
revised ordinary fare between Bengaluru (KBS) and Kanakapura is Rs 124, up from
Rs 107. The equivalent fare to Mysuru is Rs 162.

There is no published fare for the Harohalli fare stage in any source we could
reach. Scaling the published KBS-Kanakapura fare by distance gives roughly Rs 86
one way to Harohalli, but that is an estimate, not a tariff. The honest answer is:
budget about Rs 80-90 and confirm at the depot or on the KSRTC app.

metadata.heading: Published KSRTC fares on the corridor

text:
# Shakti Scheme — free travel for women

The Shakti scheme has provided free travel for women and transgender residents of
Karnataka on non-premium state buses since 11 June 2023. Key rules:

- Valid on BMTC ordinary and metro feeder services and on KSRTC ordinary and
  express services within Karnataka.
- Not valid on AC services, Vajra, Vayu Vajra, Airavat, Ambari, Rajahamsa or other
  luxury classes.
- Not valid for the out-of-state portion of an interstate journey. A woman on an
  Udupi-Kasaragod service still pays for the Kerala leg.
- Requires proof of Karnataka residence, usually Aadhaar. A Shakti smart card is
  available through Seva Sindhu but is not mandatory for most travel.

metadata.heading: Shakti Scheme — free travel for women

text:
# Shakti Scheme — free travel for women

For a woman Karnataka resident who does not need AC, Shakti makes every paid
non-AC pass redundant. It therefore dominates any cost optimisation: the correct
recommendation is to carry ID and buy nothing. Girl students do not need a separate
student pass for the same reason.

metadata.heading: Shakti Scheme — free travel for women

text:
# Choosing between BMTC, KSRTC and the metro on this corridor

- If both ends are inside the BMTC network, use BMTC. Fares are lower and the
  ordinary monthly pass or free student pass applies.
- If one end is beyond the BMTC network, a KSRTC ordinary leg is usually needed.
  A KSRTC student pass or the free student pass covers it.
- The metro reaches Silk Institute on the Green Line, which is the closest metro
  station to the Kanakapura Road corridor. From Silk Institute onward you still
  need a bus, so a metro-plus-bus commute is only competitive for trips that start
  on the Green Line.

metadata.heading: Choosing between BMTC, KSRTC and the metro on this corridor

text:
# BMTC ordinary bus fare slabs (revised 5 January 2025)

BMTC fares are charged by fare stage, not by route. The published revised slabs for
ordinary non-AC services are:

| Distance | Adult fare |
|---|---|
| First 2 km | Rs 6 |
| Up to 4 km | Rs 12 |
| Up to 6 km | Rs 18 |
| 8-10 km | Rs 23 |
| 12-14 km | Rs 24 |
| 16-18 km | Rs 28 |
| 20-40 km | Rs 30 |
| Up to 50 km | Rs 32 (maximum ordinary fare) |

Senior citizens pay a concessional fare (Rs 5 for the first 2 km, Rs 24 at 50 km).
Children pay about half. The fare tables in the GTFS feed carry their own
stage-to-stage prices, and those take precedence when a stage pair is present.

metadata.heading: BMTC ordinary bus fare slabs (revised 5 January 2025)

# BMTC pass prices (revised 9 January 2025)

| Pass | Price | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Daily pass (ordinary) | Rs 80 | Up from Rs 70 |
| Weekly pass (ordinary) | Rs 350 | Up from Rs 300 |
| Monthly pass (ordinary) | Rs 1,200 | Up from Rs 1,050 |
| Ordinary extension monthly pass | Rs 1,500 | For newly extended routes beyond 40 km |
| Vajra AC daily pass | Rs 140 | Up from Rs 120 |
| Vajra AC monthly pass | Rs 2,000 | Up from Rs 1,800 |

| Student pass (non-AC) | Free since 12 June 2026 | State free student pass scheme |

# Namma Metro fares

BMRCL charges distance-based single-journey fares. In the GTFS feed the token
products range from Rs 10 for a short hop to Rs 90 for the longest journey across
the network. Fares are higher at peak hours for some products. There is no student
monthly pass in the published BMRCL fare products, so a student commute that mixes
metro and bus pays the metro leg in full even when the bus leg is free.

Metro lines, as of the 2026-27 GTFS feed:
- Green Line: Madavara to Silk Institute, 32 stations.
- Purple Line: Whitefield (Kadugodi) to Challaghatta.
- Yellow Line: Rashtreeya Vidyalaya Road to Delta Electronics Bommasandra.

# Namma Metro fares

Interchanges matter for routing: Majestic connects Green and Purple, and RV Road
connects Green and Yellow.

# What a student actually pays in 2026-27

Three rules decide almost every case:

1. A girl student who is a Karnataka resident pays nothing on non-AC BMTC and KSRTC
   buses, under Shakti. She may still need a metro ticket or an AC pass.
2. Any other student pays nothing on non-AC BMTC and KSRTC services under the free
   student pass, once the pass is issued. Until the card is issued, they pay normal
   fares.
3. Anyone using AC services pays the AC fare or buys the AC pass: Rs 1,400 per month
   for students, Rs 2,000 for other commuters, Rs 4,000 for the Vayu Vajra Gold pass.

metadata.heading: What a student actually pays in 2026-27

text:
# Worked example: Jayanagar to DSU Harohalli

The trip is roughly 38 km by road. Route 213-V runs Harohalli to Sanjay Gandhi
Hospital through Jayanagar, so it is a one-seat ride for many students along the
corridor. At the published ordinary slab, a 38 km trip falls in the 20-40 km band,
so the single fare is about Rs 30. A return trip is about Rs 60. Over 24 travel
days that is about Rs 1,440 a month.

metadata.heading: Worked example: Jayanagar to DSU Harohalli

# Worked example: Jayanagar to DSU Harohalli

Against that: the free student pass costs nothing for a non-AC commuter, so it saves
the full Rs 1,440. The AC student pass at Rs 1,400 would only break even if the
student actually used AC buses, and route 213-V is a non-AC ordinary service.
A non-student commuter compares Rs 1,440 against the Rs 1,200 ordinary monthly
pass, which saves about Rs 240.

text:
# Common fare questions

- Toll charges are not included in BMTC passes. Buses using NICE Road tolls charge
  the toll separately.
- Vayu Vajra airport fares are much higher than city fares and are not covered by
  ordinary or Vajra passes.
- Fare amounts change by government notification, usually with a 15 per cent
  revision. Any quoted fare should carry the date it was last verified.

# Before you start

Have these ready: Aadhaar number, a mobile number linked to Aadhaar for OTP,
the current-year fee receipt, an institution-signed pass form, a passport-size
photograph, and a caste certificate with RD number if you are an SC/ST applicant.
Decide which counter you will collect the pass from, because the form asks for it.

# The application, step by step

1. Open the Seva Sindhu / e-District portal at sevaone.karnataka.gov.in.
2. Register or log in. Aadhaar-based login with an OTP to the linked mobile is the
   usual route; a user account with password also works.
3. Choose "Apply for Services", then "View all available services", and search for
   the student bus pass service for the current academic year.
4. Pick the operator: BMTC for city travel, KSRTC for a mofussil corridor such as
   Kanakapura Road, or NWKRTC / KKRTC in other divisions.
5. Fill in the student's details, institution, course, year and the route between
   residence and institution.
6. Download the generated application form. Print it, get it signed and stamped by
   the institution, scan it, and upload it.
7. Upload the supporting documents. Keep each file under the portal's size limit
   and in the requested format.
8. Select the pass-issuing counter and submit.
9. Track the application with the acknowledgement number. On approval an SMS gives
   the counter and collection window.
10. Collect the smart card in person. A live photograph is taken at the counter.

# Timelines

Applications normally open in late May and passes are issued from 1 June, staggered
by category: school and PUC passes first, degree and professional courses from
July, technical and medical courses from August. A student who applies in October is
late but not excluded; the pass is still issued for the remainder of the academic
year.

# If the portal rejects the application

- **"Institution not found"** — the institution's DISE or AISHE code is missing from
  the dropdown. Ask the college office for the exact code and try the nearest
  matching entry, or apply at a Bangalore One counter.
- **"Aadhaar authentication failed"** — the mobile number linked to Aadhaar is stale.
  Update it at an Aadhaar centre, then retry. Do not create a second account.
- **"Document not clear"** — rescan at a higher resolution. Photographs taken at an
  angle or with a shadow are the usual cause.
- **"Category mismatch"** — the course category selected does not match the fee
  receipt. Correct the category, not the receipt.
- **"Counter unavailable"** — the chosen counter does not handle that category. Pick
  another from the list.

metadata.heading: If the portal rejects the application

text:
# If you already paid

Students who paid for a 2026-27 pass before the free scheme took effect should claim
a refund on Seva Sindhu: log in with the registered mobile and OTP, complete Aadhaar
e-KYC, and submit bank account details. KSRTC has said refunds are credited within
seven days of applying. Keep the old pass until the refund arrives; it stays valid
until then.

# Help and escalation

- Seva Sindhu helpline: 080-24410574. Email: sevasindhu@karnataka.gov.in.
- BMTC pass counters: Majestic (Kempegowda Bus Station), Kengeri, Shantinagar,
  Hosakote, Electronic City and Anekal are the commonly used Bengaluru counters.
- KSRTC publishes the list of its pass-issuing counters for each academic year;
  there were 123 counters for 2026-27.
- For a corridor-specific KSRTC season ticket, ask at the depot that operates the
  route, not at a BMTC counter.

# What to do if the pass has not arrived before term starts

Buy single tickets and keep the receipts. Most corporations reimburse pass-period
travel if the delay is caused by the corporation or the portal, but only with
receipts and a written complaint. Photograph every ticket or keep the UPI messages.

text:
# What the metro covers

Three lines carry passengers today:

- **Green Line** — Madavara to Silk Institute, 32 stations. This is the line that
  matters most for the Kanakapura Road corridor: Silk Institute is its southern
  terminus and the closest metro station to Harohalli.
- **Purple Line** — Whitefield (Kadugodi) to Challaghatta, running east-west through
  Majestic.
- **Yellow Line** — Rashtreeya Vidyalaya Road to Delta Electronics Bommasandra,
  serving the Bommasandra industrial belt.

Majestic is the Green-Purple interchange. RV Road is the Green-Yellow interchange.

# What the metro covers

A fourth line, the **Pink Line** (Kalena Agrahara to Nagawara), is built but **not yet
carrying passengers**. Its 7.5 km elevated section from Kalena Agrahara to Tavarekere
(6 stations) completed the final CMRS safety inspection on 8 October 2026 and is
awaiting authorisation, with services expected in late October or early November 2026.
The 13.76 km underground section from Dairy Circle to Nagawara (12 stations) is
targeted for early 2027. The full line is 21.26 km with 18 stations. When it opens it
will interchange with the Yellow Line at Jayadeva Hospital and with the Purple Line at
MG Road, and will give Bannerghatta Road, JP Nagar, Shivajinagar and Nagawara a direct
north-south metro spine. Until then, no journey should be planned on it.

# Metro fares and ticketing

Metro fares range from Rs 10 for a short hop to Rs 90 for the longest journey across
the network, in Rs 10 steps. In the BMRCL feed the fare between any two stations is
determined entirely by how many stations the journey spans: 1-2 stops Rs 10, 3-4 Rs 20,
5-6 Rs 30, 7-8 Rs 40, 9-10 Rs 50, 11-15 Rs 60, 16-20 Rs 70, 21-25 Rs 80, and 26 or more
stops Rs 90. Tickets are bought as tokens, on a travel card, or through the Namma Metro
app with a QR ticket. A 5 per cent fare revision announced for 9 February 2026 was kept
in abeyance and has not been implemented, so the Rs 10-90 table remains in force.

# Metro fares and ticketing

There is no student monthly pass among BMRCL's published fare products. The state
free student pass scheme covers the four road transport corporations, not the metro,
so the metro leg of a student commute is always paid. A student who travels Silk
Institute to Majestic pays the metro fare for that leg even if the bus legs on
either side are free.

# Timings

Metro services typically start around 05:00 and run until about 23:00, with
slightly later services on weekends. The GTFS feed carries per-trip timings, but
BMRCL does not publish per-stop times for intermediate stations; the feed's
intermediate times are estimated from stop spacing and average speed and can be a
couple of minutes out.

# Combining bus and metro

The useful pattern for a long commute is: feeder bus or short BMTC ride to the
nearest metro station, metro across the city, then a bus from the metro station
nearest the destination. For the Harohalli corridor the practical version is:

1. BMTC or KSRTC ordinary bus from the student's locality to Silk Institute metro
   station, which sits at 12.8616 N, 77.5299 E.
2. Green Line north to Majestic if the destination is central.
3. A BMTC bus from Majestic to the final destination.

# Combining bus and metro

This only beats a single-seat bus when the destination is near a metro line and the
bus route is congested. For a DSU Harohalli student whose home is on the Kanakapura
Road side, route 213-V straight through is usually simpler than bus-metro-bus, and
it is free under the student pass.

# Metro access details

BMRCL's GTFS includes station entrances, pathways and platform levels. Stations with
multiple entrances can save a lot of walking if you pick the right one: for example,
Majestic has separate entrances for the Green and Purple platforms. The pathway data
carries traversal times, which matter when making a tight interchange.

# Auto and last-mile

Autos are outside the scope of this dataset. Auto fares in Bengaluru were last
revised separately from bus fares and are metered. For a short last-mile hop from a
metro station, walking to the nearest bus stop is usually cheaper than an auto, and
the free student pass covers the bus.

# Namma Metro fare rules and ticketing (official BMRCL)

Source: BMRCL official Fare Rules page (https://www.bmrc.co.in/fare-rules/) and the
Revised Fare Chart dated 14 February 2025, linked from https://www.bmrc.co.in/tickets/.
Retrieved 2026-10-22.

text:
# Smart card and NCMC discounts on Namma Metro

Smart card and NCMC fares are discounted from the token fare:
- Monday to Saturday: 5% during peak hours and 10% during non-peak hours.
- Sundays and national holidays (26 January, 15 August, 2 October): 10% throughout the business day.
- Non-peak hours run from the start of revenue hours to 08:00, from 12:00 to 16:00, and from 21:00 to the end of revenue hours. All other times are peak.

text:
# Namma Metro helpdesk and contact

CONTACT NAMMA METRO HELP-DESK 1800-425-12345 FOR MORE DETAILS.

# Children below 3 feet travel free

Tickets are not required for children below 3 feet. No age criteria is considered.

# Penalty for ticketless travel or a lost ticket

Penalty for ticketless travel or lost ticket is Rs.200/- apart from maximum token fare.

metadata.heading: Penalty for ticketless travel or a lost ticket

text:
# Penalty for mismatch (skipped entry or exit)

Skipping of any entry or exit is termed as MISMATCH. The penalty for mismatch is Rs10.Minimum Fare will be charged for entering into a station.

metadata.heading: Penalty for mismatch (skipped entry or exit)

text:
# Token validity and revalidation

Entry through the Automatic Gate must be made within 30 minutes of purchasing a token. After 30 minutes, an administrative charge of Rs. 5/- applies for revalidation.

# Overstay rule and penalty

A passenger holding a valid ticket can exit from paid area of same station within 20 minutes and from paid area of other stations within 120 minutes. For overstaying in paid area beyond these limits, penalty of Rs 50 per hour is charged subject to a maximum of Rs 100.

# Luggage allowance

One Luggage, with a maximum dimension of 60 cm x 45 cm x 25 cm (length x breadth x height) is allowed per person. To allow commuters to carry extra luggage/ additional baggage and oversized baggages, charges at the rate of Rs. 30/- per baggage is levied. This luggage ticket can be purchased from Customer Care Center(CCC).

# Penalty for unpaid luggage

If ticket is not purchased for the additional baggage, then a penalty of Rs.250/- will be imposed. In case of any dispute, notwithstanding that commuter holds a valid ticket for travel, will be liable to be removed from the train by any metro railway officials authorised by the metro railway administration in this behalf or by any other person whom such metro railway official may call to his aid.

# Smart card validity extension

Add-value in the Smart Card shall be valid for ten years from the date of last add-value. The validity extension can be done by paying administrative charges of Rs. 20/- at Customer Care Center of any station.

# How many tokens one passenger may buy

The maximum number of tokens which are to be issued by the Ticket office operator to a single passenger at a time is six.

### 1. How much does a BMTC student bus pass cost in 2026-27?
Nothing, for non-AC services. Under the state free student bus pass scheme effective
12 June 2026, the government pays the pass fee. Applying online on Seva Sindhu is
free; a Bangalore One counter may charge a Rs 30 service fee for data entry.

metadata.heading: 1. How much does a BMTC student bus pass cost in 2026-27?

text:
### 2. Is the student pass really free, or is it a discount?
It is free for non-AC BMTC and KSRTC services. The government also pays a Rs 100
processing fee per pass and Rs 50 towards the accident relief fund. AC services are
not covered, so an AC student pass still costs money.

metadata.heading: 2. Is the student pass really free, or is it a discount?

text:
### 3. What did the student pass cost before the free scheme?
For 2025-26: primary Rs 150, high-school boys Rs 750, high-school girls Rs 550, PUC
Rs 1,050, degree and professional Rs 1,300, technical and medical Rs 1,830, and
SC/ST students Rs 150.

metadata.heading: 3. What did the student pass cost before the free scheme?

text:
### 4. How much is the BMTC AC (Vajra) student pass?
Rs 1,400 per month, following the January 2025 revision. It covers BMTC AC services
but not the Vayu Vajra airport buses.

metadata.heading: 4. How much is the BMTC AC (Vajra) student pass?

text:
### 5. How much is a normal BMTC monthly pass for a non-student?
Rs 1,200 per calendar month for ordinary non-AC services, revised from Rs 1,050 in
January 2025. There is a Rs 1,500 extension pass for newly extended routes beyond
40 km.

metadata.heading: 5. How much is a normal BMTC monthly pass for a non-student?

text:
### 6. What does the Vayu Vajra Gold pass cost?
Rs 4,000 per month. It is the only pass that covers airport services, and it
includes toll and GST components.

metadata.heading: 6. What does the Vayu Vajra Gold pass cost?

text:
### 7. Is there a Namma Metro student pass?
No student pass appears in BMRCL's published fare products. Metro fares are
distance-based, roughly Rs 10 to Rs 90 per journey, and the state free student pass
scheme does not cover the metro.

metadata.heading: 7. Is there a Namma Metro student pass?

text:
### 8. Do I need a pass if I am a woman?
No, if you are a Karnataka resident travelling on non-AC services. The Shakti scheme
gives free travel on BMTC ordinary and KSRTC ordinary or express buses inside
Karnataka. Carry an ID. You would only need a pass for AC or metro travel.

metadata.heading: 8. Do I need a pass if I am a woman?

text:
### 9. Does Shakti work on AC buses?
No. Shakti is limited to non-premium, non-AC services. Vajra, Vayu Vajra, Airavat,
Ambari and Rajahamsa are excluded.

metadata.heading: 9. Does Shakti work on AC buses?

text:
### 10. Does the free student pass cover AC buses?
No. It covers non-AC services of BMTC, KSRTC, NWKRTC and KKRTC only.

metadata.heading: 10. Does the free student pass cover AC buses?

text:
### 11. I already paid for my 2026-27 pass. Can I get a refund?
Yes. Claim it on Seva Sindhu with Aadhaar e-KYC and bank details. KSRTC has said
refunds are credited within seven days. Keep using the old pass until the refund
arrives.

metadata.heading: 11. I already paid for my 2026-27 pass. Can I get a refund?

text:
### 12. Is there a daily or weekly option?
Yes. BMTC ordinary daily pass Rs 80 and weekly pass Rs 350, both revised in January
2025. A Vajra AC daily pass is Rs 140.

## Documents and applications

metadata.heading: 12. Is there a daily or weekly option?

text:
### 13. What documents do I need for a student pass?
An institution-signed application form, the current-year fee receipt or bonafide
certificate, Aadhaar, a passport-size photograph, and a caste certificate with RD
number if you are SC/ST. A live photo is taken at the counter.

metadata.heading: 13. What documents do I need for a student pass?

text:
### 14. Do I have to apply, or is the pass automatic?
You must apply. The free pass is not issued automatically to anyone.

metadata.heading: 14. Do I have to apply, or is the pass automatic?

text:
### 15. Where do I apply?
On Seva Sindhu (sevaone.karnataka.gov.in). You can also apply at Bangalore One,
Karnataka One or Grama One centres for a Rs 30 service charge.

### 16. Can my parent collect the pass for me?
No. The student must collect the smart card in person because a live photograph is
captured and printed on the card.

metadata.heading: 16. Can my parent collect the pass for me?

text:
### 17. How long is the pass valid?
The academic year. School and PUC passes run roughly June to March; degree and
professional courses July to June; technical and medical courses August to July. ITI
passes run 12 months.

metadata.heading: 17. How long is the pass valid?

text:
### 18. What if my college is more than 40 km from home?
You may be asked for a declaration that the course is not available at a closer
institution. KSRTC's distance norm is up to 60 km one-way. Students on the
Kanakapura Road corridor often fall in this band.

metadata.heading: 18. What if my college is more than 40 km from home?

text:
### 19. My application was rejected because the institution was not in the list. What now?
The institution's DISE or AISHE code is missing. Get the exact code from the college
office, or apply through a Bangalore One counter where the operator can enter it
manually.

metadata.heading: 19. My application was rejected because the institution was not in the list. What now?

text:
### 20. My Aadhaar OTP is not arriving. What should I do?
The mobile number linked to Aadhaar is probably stale. Update it at an Aadhaar
centre and retry. Do not create a second Seva Sindhu account.

metadata.heading: 20. My Aadhaar OTP is not arriving. What should I do?

text:
### 21. Can I apply for a pass mid-year?
Yes. The pass is issued for the remaining part of the academic year. Applying in
October is late but allowed.

metadata.heading: 21. Can I apply for a pass mid-year?

text:
### 22. What do I do if I lose my pass card?
Apply for a replacement at the issuing counter. BMTC charges a fixed replacement
fee, historically Rs 100, and the same fee applies to a route change.

## Routes and travel

text:
### 23. Which bus goes from Jayanagar to DSU Harohalli?
Route 213-V runs Harohalli to Sanjay Gandhi Hospital through Jayanagar, so it is a
one-seat ride for much of the corridor. Route 213-VD connects Dayananda Sagara MDC
with Banashankari and Anjanapura. Both are ordinary non-AC services.

metadata.heading: 23. Which bus goes from Jayanagar to DSU Harohalli?

text:
### 24. How do I get to DSU Harohalli from Majestic?
Take a Banashankari-bound bus or the Green Line metro to Banashankari, then a 213-V
or 213-VD toward Harohalli. Ask for the Dayananda Sagara MDC stop, which is at the
campus gate.

metadata.heading: 24. How do I get to DSU Harohalli from Majestic?

text:
### 25. Which stop is closest to the DSU Harohalli campus?
Dayananda Sagara MDC (BMTC stop code HRHD) at about 12.663 N, 77.450 E is the campus
stop. BWSSB Quaters Harohalli (BWSSBQ) is a short walk away on the main road.

metadata.heading: 25. Which stop is closest to the DSU Harohalli campus?

text:
### 26. Is there a direct bus from Banashankari to Harohalli?
Yes. Route 213-VD runs between Dayananda Sagara MDC and Banashankari Bus Station,
about 59 stops, roughly 38 km.

metadata.heading: 26. Is there a direct bus from Banashankari to Harohalli?

text:
### 27. How long is the Jayanagar to Harohalli bus ride?
About 90 minutes to two hours in peak traffic for roughly 38 km. The distance is not
the problem on this corridor; the traffic is.

metadata.heading: 27. How long is the Jayanagar to Harohalli bus ride?

text:
### 28. Does the metro go to Harohalli?
No. The Green Line ends at Silk Institute, about 12 km north of Harohalli. From
there you need a bus.

metadata.heading: 28. Does the metro go to Harohalli?

text:
### 29. Which metro station is closest to Harohalli?
Silk Institute on the Green Line, at 12.8616 N, 77.5299 E.

metadata.heading: 29. Which metro station is closest to Harohalli?

text:
### 30. What is the KSRTC fare from Bengaluru to Kanakapura?
Rs 124 for an ordinary bus, revised on 5 January 2025 from Rs 107.

metadata.heading: 30. What is the KSRTC fare from Bengaluru to Kanakapura?

text:
### 31. What is the KSRTC fare to Harohalli?
There is no published fare for the Harohalli stage. Scaling the Kanakapura fare by
distance suggests roughly Rs 80-90, but treat that as an estimate and confirm at the
depot or on the KSRTC app.

metadata.heading: 31. What is the KSRTC fare to Harohalli?

text:
### 32. Can I use my BMTC student pass on a KSRTC bus?
Not unless the pass is a KSRTC pass. BMTC and KSRTC are separate corporations. Since
2026-27 the state free student pass covers non-AC services of both, but the pass
must be issued for the operator and route you use.

metadata.heading: 32. Can I use my BMTC student pass on a KSRTC bus?

text:
### 33. Do KSRTC monthly season tickets cover express buses?
A pass issued for Express services is valid on Express and Ordinary services. A pass
issued for Ordinary services is valid only on Ordinary services.

## Costs and comparisons

metadata.heading: 33. Do KSRTC monthly season tickets cover express buses?

text:
### 34. Is a monthly pass worth it if I spend Rs 60 a day on buses?
At Rs 60 a day for 24 days you spend Rs 1,440 a month. The ordinary monthly pass is
Rs 1,200, so you save Rs 240. If you are a student, the free pass makes it a
no-brainer: you save the full Rs 1,440.

metadata.heading: 34. Is a monthly pass worth it if I spend Rs 60 a day on buses?

text:
### 35. Is the AC pass worth Rs 1,400 for a student?
Only if you actually use AC buses. Rs 1,400 is about 47 ordinary rides at Rs 30, so
you need roughly 24 AC journeys a month to break even. On route 213-V, which is
ordinary, the AC pass would be wasted money.

metadata.heading: 35. Is the AC pass worth Rs 1,400 for a student?

text:
### 36. How much does a typical student commute cost per month?
A 38 km one-way trip at the ordinary slab is about Rs 30. Return trips for 24 days
come to about Rs 1,440. Under the free student pass, that becomes Rs 0.

metadata.heading: 36. How much does a typical student commute cost per month?

text:
### 37. Are tolls included in passes?
No. BMTC passes exclude toll charges on roads such as NICE Road; you pay the toll
separately.

### 38. Do senior citizens get a discount?
Yes. BMTC senior citizen fares are concessional, roughly Rs 5 for the first 2 km and
Rs 24 at 50 km. A senior citizen ordinary monthly pass also exists.

## Data and reliability

metadata.heading: 38. Do senior citizens get a discount?

text:
### 39. How current is the route and fare information?
Stop and route data comes from the BMTC and BMRCL GTFS feeds, valid through
September 2027 for BMTC and August 2027 for the metro. Pass and fare rules were last
verified on 22 October 2026. Fares change by government notification, so always
check the official portal before paying.

metadata.heading: 39. How current is the route and fare information?

text:
### 40. Why does the agent sometimes refuse to quote a price?
Because some prices are not published in any accessible source. KSRTC corridor
season tickets and business-class fares are priced at the depot. It is better to
say "I cannot confirm this, here is the official link" than to invent a number you
would then budget around.

metadata.heading: 40. Why does the agent sometimes refuse to quote a price?

# CampusTransit FAQ — 40 questions students actually ask

## Passes and prices

### 1. How much does a BMTC student bus pass cost in 2026-27?
Nothing, for non-AC services. Under the state free student bus pass scheme effective
12 June 2026, the government pays the pass fee. Applying online on Seva Sindhu is
free; a Bangalore One counter may charge a Rs 30 service fee for data entry.

### 2. Is the student pass really free, or is it a discount?
It is free for non-AC BMTC and KSRTC services. The government also pays a Rs 100
processing fee per pass and Rs 50 towards the accident relief fund. AC services are
not covered, so an AC student pass still costs money.

### 3. What did the student pass cost before the free scheme?
For 2025-26: primary Rs 150, high-school boys Rs 750, high-school girls Rs 550, PUC
Rs 1,050, degree and professional Rs 1,300, technical and medical Rs 1,830, and
SC/ST students Rs 150.

### 4. How much is the BMTC AC (Vajra) student pass?
Rs 1,400 per month, following the January 2025 revision. It covers BMTC AC services
but not the Vayu Vajra airport buses.

### 5. How much is a normal BMTC monthly pass for a non-student?
Rs 1,200 per calendar month for ordinary non-AC services, revised from Rs 1,050 in
January 2025. There is a Rs 1,500 extension pass for newly extended routes beyond
40 km.

### 6. What does the Vayu Vajra Gold pass cost?
Rs 4,000 per month. It is the only pass that covers airport services, and it
includes toll and GST components.

### 7. Is there a Namma Metro student pass?

SOURCE FILE: curated/faq.md

No student pass appears in BMRCL's published fare products. Metro fares are
distance-based, roughly Rs 10 to Rs 90 per journey, and the state free student pass
scheme does not cover the metro.

### 8. Do I need a pass if I am a woman?
No, if you are a Karnataka resident travelling on non-AC services. The Shakti scheme
gives free travel on BMTC ordinary and KSRTC ordinary or express buses inside
Karnataka. Carry an ID. You would only need a pass for AC or metro travel.

### 9. Does Shakti work on AC buses?
No. Shakti is limited to non-premium, non-AC services. Vajra, Vayu Vajra, Airavat,
Ambari and Rajahamsa are excluded.

### 10. Does the free student pass cover AC buses?
No. It covers non-AC services of BMTC, KSRTC, NWKRTC and KKRTC only.

### 11. I already paid for my 2026-27 pass. Can I get a refund?
Yes. Claim it on Seva Sindhu with Aadhaar e-KYC and bank details. KSRTC has said
refunds are credited within seven days. Keep using the old pass until the refund
arrives.

### 12. Is there a daily or weekly option?
Yes. BMTC ordinary daily pass Rs 80 and weekly pass Rs 350, both revised in January
2025. A Vajra AC daily pass is Rs 140.

## Documents and applications

### 13. What documents do I need for a student pass?
An institution-signed application form, the current-year fee receipt or bonafide
certificate, Aadhaar, a passport-size photograph, and a caste certificate with RD
number if you are SC/ST. A live photo is taken at the counter.

### 14. Do I have to apply, or is the pass automatic?
You must apply. The free pass is not issued automatically to anyone.

SOURCE FILE: curated/faq.md

### 15. Where do I apply?
On Seva Sindhu (sevaone.karnataka.gov.in). You can also apply at Bangalore One,
Karnataka One or Grama One centres for a Rs 30 service charge.

### 16. Can my parent collect the pass for me?
No. The student must collect the smart card in person because a live photograph is
captured and printed on the card.

### 17. How long is the pass valid?
The academic year. School and PUC passes run roughly June to March; degree and
professional courses July to June; technical and medical courses August to July. ITI
passes run 12 months.

### 18. What if my college is more than 40 km from home?
You may be asked for a declaration that the course is not available at a closer
institution. KSRTC's distance norm is up to 60 km one-way. Students on the
Kanakapura Road corridor often fall in this band.

### 19. My application was rejected because the institution was not in the list. What now?
The institution's DISE or AISHE code is missing. Get the exact code from the college
office, or apply through a Bangalore One counter where the operator can enter it
manually.

### 20. My Aadhaar OTP is not arriving. What should I do?
The mobile number linked to Aadhaar is probably stale. Update it at an Aadhaar
centre and retry. Do not create a second Seva Sindhu account.

### 21. Can I apply for a pass mid-year?
Yes. The pass is issued for the remaining part of the academic year. Applying in
October is late but allowed.

### 22. What do I do if I lose my pass card?
Apply for a replacement at the issuing counter. BMTC charges a fixed replacement

fee, historically Rs 100, and the same fee applies to a route change.

## Routes and travel

### 23. Which bus goes from Jayanagar to DSU Harohalli?
Route 213-V runs Harohalli to Sanjay Gandhi Hospital through Jayanagar, so it is a
one-seat ride for much of the corridor. Route 213-VD connects Dayananda Sagara MDC
with Banashankari and Anjanapura. Both are ordinary non-AC services.

### 24. How do I get to DSU Harohalli from Majestic?
Take a Banashankari-bound bus or the Green Line metro to Banashankari, then a 213-V
or 213-VD toward Harohalli. Ask for the Dayananda Sagara MDC stop, which is at the
campus gate.

### 25. Which stop is closest to the DSU Harohalli campus?
Dayananda Sagara MDC (BMTC stop code HRHD) at about 12.663 N, 77.450 E is the campus
stop. BWSSB Quaters Harohalli (BWSSBQ) is a short walk away on the main road.

### 26. Is there a direct bus from Banashankari to Harohalli?
Yes. Route 213-VD runs between Dayananda Sagara MDC and Banashankari Bus Station,
about 59 stops, roughly 38 km.

### 27. How long is the Jayanagar to Harohalli bus ride?
About 90 minutes to two hours in peak traffic for roughly 38 km. The distance is not
the problem on this corridor; the traffic is.

### 28. Does the metro go to Harohalli?
No. The Green Line ends at Silk Institute, about 12 km north of Harohalli. From
there you need a bus.

### 29. Which metro station is closest to Harohalli?
Silk Institute on the Green Line, at 12.8616 N, 77.5299 E.

### 30. What is the KSRTC fare from Bengaluru to Kanakapura?
Rs 124 for an ordinary bus, revised on 5 January 2025 from Rs 107.

SOURCE FILE: curated/faq.md

### 31. What is the KSRTC fare to Harohalli?
There is no published fare for the Harohalli stage. Scaling the Kanakapura fare by
distance suggests roughly Rs 80-90, but treat that as an estimate and confirm at the
depot or on the KSRTC app.

### 32. Can I use my BMTC student pass on a KSRTC bus?
Not unless the pass is a KSRTC pass. BMTC and KSRTC are separate corporations. Since
2026-27 the state free student pass covers non-AC services of both, but the pass
must be issued for the operator and route you use.

### 33. Do KSRTC monthly season tickets cover express buses?
A pass issued for Express services is valid on Express and Ordinary services. A pass
issued for Ordinary services is valid only on Ordinary services.

## Costs and comparisons

### 34. Is a monthly pass worth it if I spend Rs 60 a day on buses?
At Rs 60 a day for 24 days you spend Rs 1,440 a month. The ordinary monthly pass is
Rs 1,200, so you save Rs 240. If you are a student, the free pass makes it a
no-brainer: you save the full Rs 1,440.

### 35. Is the AC pass worth Rs 1,400 for a student?
Only if you actually use AC buses. Rs 1,400 is about 47 ordinary rides at Rs 30, so
you need roughly 24 AC journeys a month to break even. On route 213-V, which is
ordinary, the AC pass would be wasted money.

### 36. How much does a typical student commute cost per month?
A 38 km one-way trip at the ordinary slab is about Rs 30. Return trips for 24 days
come to about Rs 1,440. Under the free student pass, that becomes Rs 0.

### 37. Are tolls included in passes?

SOURCE FILE: curated/faq.md

No. BMTC passes exclude toll charges on roads such as NICE Road; you pay the toll
separately.

### 38. Do senior citizens get a discount?
Yes. BMTC senior citizen fares are concessional, roughly Rs 5 for the first 2 km and
Rs 24 at 50 km. A senior citizen ordinary monthly pass also exists.

## Data and reliability

### 39. How current is the route and fare information?
Stop and route data comes from the BMTC and BMRCL GTFS feeds, valid through
September 2027 for BMTC and August 2027 for the metro. Pass and fare rules were last
verified on 22 October 2026. Fares change by government notification, so always
check the official portal before paying.

### 40. Why does the agent sometimes refuse to quote a price?
Because some prices are not published in any accessible source. KSRTC corridor
season tickets and business-class fares are priced at the depot. It is better to
say "I cannot confirm this, here is the official link" than to invent a number you
would then budget around.

# BMTC and KSRTC Student Bus Passes — Basics

## Who issues what
BMTC issues student passes for travel inside Bengaluru's city network. KSRTC issues
student passes for travel on mofussil (inter-city / inter-town) services, including
the Kanakapura Road corridor that runs through Harohalli. Both corporations use the
same state application portal, Seva Sindhu, and the same broad category structure.

## Student pass categories and the pre-2026 fee structure
Pass fees depend on the course, not on the distance travelled. The published
2025-26 category fees were:

| Category | Pass fee (2025-26) | Validity |
|---|---|---|
| Primary school (classes 1-7) | Rs 150 | June 2025 - March 2026 |
| High school boys (classes 8-10) | Rs 750 | June 2025 - March 2026 |
| High school girls (classes 8-10) | Rs 550 | June 2025 - March 2026 |
| PUC (classes 11-12) | Rs 1,050 | June 2025 - March 2026 |
| PUC evening college | Rs 1,630 | June 2025 - March 2026 |
| Degree, professional, diploma (ITI) | Rs 1,300 | July 2025 - June 2026 |
| Technical and medical | Rs 1,830 | August 2025 - July 2026 |
| Evening college and PhD | Rs 1,630 | July 2025 - June 2026 |
| SC/ST students (all categories) | Rs 150 | As per category |

These published fees are now largely historical: from 12 June 2026 the state pays
the pass fee for all students on non-AC services (see the free pass document). The
figures remain useful because the *category* you fall into still decides the pass
validity window and the distance limits that apply.

## What a student pass actually covers

SOURCE FILE: curated/policy_docs/01_student_bus_pass_basics.md

A student pass covers unlimited travel on the services named on the pass, for the
validity window, between the student's residence and the institution. It is not a
city-wide travel card:

- BMTC student passes cover BMTC services inside the city network, including
  non-AC ordinary buses and metro feeder services.
- KSRTC student passes cover KSRTC ordinary services on the declared route, under
  the existing distance norm of up to 60 km one-way between residence and
  institution.
- Neither pass covers AC Vajra, Vayu Vajra airport services, Airavat, Ambari,
  Rajahamsa or other luxury classes unless the pass is explicitly an AC pass.

## Documents required
The standard document set for a student pass application is:

1. The pass application form, downloaded from Seva Sindhu and signed and stamped by
   the institution.
2. A bonafide certificate from the institution, or the current academic year's fee
   receipt, which serves as proof of enrolment.
3. Aadhaar card.
4. A passport-size photograph. For a smart-card pass, a live photograph is captured
   at the counter when the card is printed.
5. A caste certificate with an RD number, for SC/ST applicants.
6. A mobile number registered on Seva Sindhu, for OTP and collection SMS.

Students who live more than 40 km from the institution may be asked for a
declaration that the course is not available at a closer institution. This affects
many Harohalli and Kanakapura Road commuters.

## Where to apply
Applications are submitted online at the Seva Sindhu / e-District portal

(sevaone.karnataka.gov.in). Applying online is free. Students who need help can use
a Bangalore One, Karnataka One or Grama One centre for a service charge of Rs 30.
After approval, an SMS tells the student which counter to collect the smart card
from. The student must collect it in person.

BMTC collection counters include Majestic (Kempegowda Bus Station), Kengeri,
Shantinagar, Hosakote, Electronic City and Anekal. KSRTC notifies its own list of
pass-issuing counters, which for 2026-27 ran to 123 counters across Karnataka.

## Renewal, replacement and route changes
Student passes are issued for an academic year and must be renewed each year
through the same Seva Sindhu process. If a pass card is lost or damaged, or if the
student changes route, BMTC charges a fixed replacement or route-change fee
(historically Rs 100). Renewal requires the same document set plus the previous
pass.

## Common reasons applications are rejected
- The application form is not signed and stamped by the institution.
- The fee receipt belongs to a previous academic year.
- The name or date of birth does not match the Aadhaar record.
- The photograph is not a recent passport-style photograph.
- The selected collection counter does not handle the applicant's category.
- For SC/ST applicants, the caste certificate RD number is missing.

# Karnataka Free Student Bus Pass (2026-27)

## What changed
On 12 June 2026 the Karnataka Transport Department issued an order making bus
passes free for all students travelling on non-AC services of the four state road
transport corporations: BMTC, KSRTC, NWKRTC and KKRTC. The scheme was announced by
Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar in the first cabinet meeting after taking office and
implemented within days.

The state bears the pass fee, a processing fee of Rs 100 per pass and an accident
relief fund contribution of Rs 50 per pass (Rs 5 per month of accident insurance
cover). The estimated annual cost of the scheme is Rs 286.08 crore, plus about
Rs 15 crore in processing and accident-relief charges.

## Who is eligible
- Any regular student enrolled in a recognised school, PU college, degree college,
  diploma, ITI, professional course, medical course, evening college, postgraduate
  or PhD programme in Karnataka.
- Karnataka-domicile students studying in institutions in neighbouring states.
- Students from districts bordering Karnataka who study at institutions in
  Karnataka.
- Existing eligibility rules still apply: academic requirements, distance limits
  (up to 60 km one-way between residence and institution under KSRTC norms) and
  pass validity periods are unchanged.

Girls and transgender students who are Karnataka residents already travel free
under the Shakti scheme and do not need a separate student pass, although they may
still apply if they prefer to hold a card.

## What the free pass does not cover

SOURCE FILE: curated/policy_docs/02_free_student_pass_2026.md

- BMTC AC services, including Vajra and Vayu Vajra airport buses.
- KSRTC luxury classes: Airavat, Airavat Club Class, Ambari, Ambari Dream Class,
  Rajahamsa, Rajahamsa Executive, Pallakki, Flybus and EV Power Plus.
- Travel on the portion of an interstate route that leaves Karnataka.
- Namma Metro. The metro is run by BMRCL, not by the four RTCs, and is outside this
  scheme.

A student who needs AC travel must still buy the paid BMTC AC student monthly pass,
which cost Rs 1,400 per month as of the January 2025 revision.

## How to apply
1. Go to the Seva Sindhu / e-District portal at sevaone.karnataka.gov.in and log in
   with Aadhaar or mobile OTP.
2. Search for the student bus pass service for the current academic year and choose
   the operator (BMTC, KSRTC, NWKRTC or KKRTC).
3. Fill in personal details, institution details, course and the residence-to-
   institution route.
4. Download the application form, get it signed and stamped by the institution, and
   upload it with the current-year fee receipt, photograph, Aadhaar and, for SC/ST
   applicants, the caste certificate with RD number.
5. Select a convenient pass-issuing counter.
6. On approval, an SMS gives the counter address. Collect the smart card in person;
   a live photograph is taken for the card.

Applying online is free. Applications submitted through Bangalore One, Karnataka
One or Grama One centres attract the usual Rs 30 service charge.

## Refunds for passes already bought
Students who had already paid for a 2026-27 pass between 29 May and 9 June 2026 -

SOURCE FILE: curated/policy_docs/02_free_student_pass_2026.md

19,792 passes were issued in that window - are entitled to a full refund. Refunds
are claimed on Seva Sindhu with Aadhaar-based e-KYC and bank account details, and
KSRTC has said the money is credited within seven days of applying. Students who
already hold a paid pass can continue to use it until the refund is processed.

## Practical implications for a Harohalli commuter
A student commuting from Jayanagar, Banashankari or Kanakapura Road to the DSU
Harohalli campus, which is roughly 35-45 km from most of Bengaluru, is exactly the
profile this scheme is aimed at. Before June 2026 the same trip needed either a
KSRTC student pass (Rs 1,050 for a college student, 10 months) or a BMTC pass plus
a KSRTC extension, plus daily tickets for the gaps. From 2026-27 the non-AC pass
costs the student nothing, so the only paid alternatives worth considering are the
AC passes and the metro.

## Verification advice
The scheme is recent and the rules are still settling. Students should confirm the
current syllabus of fees, counter list and eligibility on Seva Sindhu before paying
anything at a counter. Any agent that quotes an exact fee without checking the
portal is guessing.

# KSRTC Travel, the Kanakapura Road Corridor, and the Shakti Scheme

## Why KSRTC matters for a Harohalli commute
Harohalli sits about 35-45 km south of central Bengaluru on the Kanakapura Road
corridor, outside the core BBMP area. BMTC does run services this far out: route
213-V (Harohalli to Sanjay Gandhi Hospital), 213-VD (Dayananda Sagara MDC to
Banashankari / Anjanapura) and 213-VB (Bannikuppe Circle / Harohalli Industrial
Area) all reach Harohalli in the GTFS feed. But the corridor is also served by
KSRTC ordinary buses running between Bengaluru (Kempegowda Bus Station) and
Kanakapura, and those buses continue south to Malavalli and Mysuru.

## KSRTC pass rules
KSRTC issues monthly season tickets between two named places on a daily-commute
basis. The rules that matter:

- Monthly passes are issued for travel along with a KSRTC photo-identity card,
  which costs Rs 50 and is valid for one year.
- A pass issued for Express services is valid on both Express and Ordinary
  services. A pass issued for Ordinary services is valid only on Ordinary services.
- Season tickets are personal and not transferable.
- Student concessional passes are the cheapest option where they apply, and since
  2026-27 they are free for non-AC services under the state scheme.

KSRTC does not publish a single statewide fare table for season tickets. Each
depot prices a pass by the corridor and the number of fare stages. The agent must
never invent a KSRTC monthly pass price; it should quote the corridor and send the
student to the depot.

## Published KSRTC fares on the corridor

SOURCE FILE: curated/policy_docs/03_ksrtc_and_shakti.md

Karnataka raised all RTC fares by 15 per cent with effect from 5 January 2025. The
revised ordinary fare between Bengaluru (KBS) and Kanakapura is Rs 124, up from
Rs 107. The equivalent fare to Mysuru is Rs 162.

There is no published fare for the Harohalli fare stage in any source we could
reach. Scaling the published KBS-Kanakapura fare by distance gives roughly Rs 86
one way to Harohalli, but that is an estimate, not a tariff. The honest answer is:
budget about Rs 80-90 and confirm at the depot or on the KSRTC app.

## Shakti Scheme — free travel for women
The Shakti scheme has provided free travel for women and transgender residents of
Karnataka on non-premium state buses since 11 June 2023. Key rules:

- Valid on BMTC ordinary and metro feeder services and on KSRTC ordinary and
  express services within Karnataka.
- Not valid on AC services, Vajra, Vayu Vajra, Airavat, Ambari, Rajahamsa or other
  luxury classes.
- Not valid for the out-of-state portion of an interstate journey. A woman on an
  Udupi-Kasaragod service still pays for the Kerala leg.
- Requires proof of Karnataka residence, usually Aadhaar. A Shakti smart card is
  available through Seva Sindhu but is not mandatory for most travel.

For a woman Karnataka resident who does not need AC, Shakti makes every paid
non-AC pass redundant. It therefore dominates any cost optimisation: the correct
recommendation is to carry ID and buy nothing. Girl students do not need a separate
student pass for the same reason.

## Choosing between BMTC, KSRTC and the metro on this corridor

SOURCE FILE: curated/policy_docs/03_ksrtc_and_shakti.md

- If both ends are inside the BMTC network, use BMTC. Fares are lower and the
  ordinary monthly pass or free student pass applies.
- If one end is beyond the BMTC network, a KSRTC ordinary leg is usually needed.
  A KSRTC student pass or the free student pass covers it.
- The metro reaches Silk Institute on the Green Line, which is the closest metro
  station to the Kanakapura Road corridor. From Silk Institute onward you still
  need a bus, so a metro-plus-bus commute is only competitive for trips that start
  on the Green Line.

# Fares, Tickets and Passes — What Costs What

## BMTC ordinary bus fare slabs (revised 5 January 2025)
BMTC fares are charged by fare stage, not by route. The published revised slabs for
ordinary non-AC services are:

| Distance | Adult fare |
|---|---|
| First 2 km | Rs 6 |
| Up to 4 km | Rs 12 |
| Up to 6 km | Rs 18 |
| 8-10 km | Rs 23 |
| 12-14 km | Rs 24 |
| 16-18 km | Rs 28 |
| 20-40 km | Rs 30 |
| Up to 50 km | Rs 32 (maximum ordinary fare) |

Senior citizens pay a concessional fare (Rs 5 for the first 2 km, Rs 24 at 50 km).
Children pay about half. The fare tables in the GTFS feed carry their own
stage-to-stage prices, and those take precedence when a stage pair is present.

## BMTC pass prices (revised 9 January 2025)
| Pass | Price | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Daily pass (ordinary) | Rs 80 | Up from Rs 70 |
| Weekly pass (ordinary) | Rs 350 | Up from Rs 300 |
| Monthly pass (ordinary) | Rs 1,200 | Up from Rs 1,050 |
| Ordinary extension monthly pass | Rs 1,500 | For newly extended routes beyond 40 km |
| Vajra AC daily pass | Rs 140 | Up from Rs 120 |
| Vajra AC monthly pass | Rs 2,000 | Up from Rs 1,800 |
| Vayu Vajra Gold monthly pass | Rs 4,000 | Includes airport services, toll and GST |
| Student monthly pass (AC) | Rs 1,400 | Up from Rs 1,200 |
| Student pass (non-AC) | Free since 12 June 2026 | State free student pass scheme |

## Namma Metro fares
BMRCL charges distance-based single-journey fares. In the GTFS feed the token
products range from Rs 10 for a short hop to Rs 90 for the longest journey across

SOURCE FILE: curated/policy_docs/04_fares_and_ticketing.md

the network. Fares are higher at peak hours for some products. There is no student
monthly pass in the published BMRCL fare products, so a student commute that mixes
metro and bus pays the metro leg in full even when the bus leg is free.

Metro lines, as of the 2026-27 GTFS feed:
- Green Line: Madavara to Silk Institute, 32 stations.
- Purple Line: Whitefield (Kadugodi) to Challaghatta.
- Yellow Line: Rashtreeya Vidyalaya Road to Delta Electronics Bommasandra.

Interchanges matter for routing: Majestic connects Green and Purple, and RV Road
connects Green and Yellow.

## What a student actually pays in 2026-27
Three rules decide almost every case:

1. A girl student who is a Karnataka resident pays nothing on non-AC BMTC and KSRTC
   buses, under Shakti. She may still need a metro ticket or an AC pass.
2. Any other student pays nothing on non-AC BMTC and KSRTC services under the free
   student pass, once the pass is issued. Until the card is issued, they pay normal
   fares.
3. Anyone using AC services pays the AC fare or buys the AC pass: Rs 1,400 per month
   for students, Rs 2,000 for other commuters, Rs 4,000 for the Vayu Vajra Gold pass.

## Worked example: Jayanagar to DSU Harohalli
The trip is roughly 38 km by road. Route 213-V runs Harohalli to Sanjay Gandhi
Hospital through Jayanagar, so it is a one-seat ride for many students along the
corridor. At the published ordinary slab, a 38 km trip falls in the 20-40 km band,
so the single fare is about Rs 30. A return trip is about Rs 60. Over 24 travel
days that is about Rs 1,440 a month.

SOURCE FILE: curated/policy_docs/04_fares_and_ticketing.md

Against that: the free student pass costs nothing for a non-AC commuter, so it saves
the full Rs 1,440. The AC student pass at Rs 1,400 would only break even if the
student actually used AC buses, and route 213-V is a non-AC ordinary service.
A non-student commuter compares Rs 1,440 against the Rs 1,200 ordinary monthly
pass, which saves about Rs 240.

## Common fare questions
- Toll charges are not included in BMTC passes. Buses using NICE Road tolls charge
  the toll separately.
- Vayu Vajra airport fares are much higher than city fares and are not covered by
  ordinary or Vajra passes.
- Fare amounts change by government notification, usually with a 15 per cent
  revision. Any quoted fare should carry the date it was last verified.

# Applying on Seva Sindhu — Step by Step, and What to Do When It Fails

## Before you start
Have these ready: Aadhaar number, a mobile number linked to Aadhaar for OTP,
the current-year fee receipt, an institution-signed pass form, a passport-size
photograph, and a caste certificate with RD number if you are an SC/ST applicant.
Decide which counter you will collect the pass from, because the form asks for it.

## The application, step by step
1. Open the Seva Sindhu / e-District portal at sevaone.karnataka.gov.in.
2. Register or log in. Aadhaar-based login with an OTP to the linked mobile is the
   usual route; a user account with password also works.
3. Choose "Apply for Services", then "View all available services", and search for
   the student bus pass service for the current academic year.
4. Pick the operator: BMTC for city travel, KSRTC for a mofussil corridor such as
   Kanakapura Road, or NWKRTC / KKRTC in other divisions.
5. Fill in the student's details, institution, course, year and the route between
   residence and institution.
6. Download the generated application form. Print it, get it signed and stamped by
   the institution, scan it, and upload it.
7. Upload the supporting documents. Keep each file under the portal's size limit
   and in the requested format.
8. Select the pass-issuing counter and submit.
9. Track the application with the acknowledgement number. On approval an SMS gives
   the counter and collection window.
10. Collect the smart card in person. A live photograph is taken at the counter.

## Timelines

SOURCE FILE: curated/policy_docs/05_applying_and_troubleshooting.md

Applications normally open in late May and passes are issued from 1 June, staggered
by category: school and PUC passes first, degree and professional courses from
July, technical and medical courses from August. A student who applies in October is
late but not excluded; the pass is still issued for the remainder of the academic
year.

## If the portal rejects the application
- **"Institution not found"** — the institution's DISE or AISHE code is missing from
  the dropdown. Ask the college office for the exact code and try the nearest
  matching entry, or apply at a Bangalore One counter.
- **"Aadhaar authentication failed"** — the mobile number linked to Aadhaar is stale.
  Update it at an Aadhaar centre, then retry. Do not create a second account.
- **"Document not clear"** — rescan at a higher resolution. Photographs taken at an
  angle or with a shadow are the usual cause.
- **"Category mismatch"** — the course category selected does not match the fee
  receipt. Correct the category, not the receipt.
- **"Counter unavailable"** — the chosen counter does not handle that category. Pick
  another from the list.

## If you already paid
Students who paid for a 2026-27 pass before the free scheme took effect should claim
a refund on Seva Sindhu: log in with the registered mobile and OTP, complete Aadhaar
e-KYC, and submit bank account details. KSRTC has said refunds are credited within
seven days of applying. Keep the old pass until the refund arrives; it stays valid
until then.

## Help and escalation
- Seva Sindhu helpline: 080-24410574. Email: sevasindhu@karnataka.gov.in.

SOURCE FILE: curated/policy_docs/05_applying_and_troubleshooting.md

- BMTC pass counters: Majestic (Kempegowda Bus Station), Kengeri, Shantinagar,
  Hosakote, Electronic City and Anekal are the commonly used Bengaluru counters.
- KSRTC publishes the list of its pass-issuing counters for each academic year;
  there were 123 counters for 2026-27.
- For a corridor-specific KSRTC season ticket, ask at the depot that operates the
  route, not at a BMTC counter.

## What to do if the pass has not arrived before term starts
Buy single tickets and keep the receipts. Most corporations reimburse pass-period
travel if the delay is caused by the corporation or the portal, but only with
receipts and a written complaint. Photograph every ticket or keep the UPI messages.

# Namma Metro and Multi-Modal Commutes

## What the metro covers
Three lines carry passengers today:

- **Green Line** — Madavara to Silk Institute, 32 stations. This is the line that
  matters most for the Kanakapura Road corridor: Silk Institute is its southern
  terminus and the closest metro station to Harohalli.
- **Purple Line** — Whitefield (Kadugodi) to Challaghatta, running east-west through
  Majestic.
- **Yellow Line** — Rashtreeya Vidyalaya Road to Delta Electronics Bommasandra,
  serving the Bommasandra industrial belt.

Majestic is the Green-Purple interchange. RV Road is the Green-Yellow interchange.

A fourth line, the **Pink Line** (Kalena Agrahara to Nagawara), is built but **not yet
carrying passengers**. Its 7.5 km elevated section from Kalena Agrahara to Tavarekere
(6 stations) completed the final CMRS safety inspection on 8 October 2026 and is
awaiting authorisation, with services expected in late October or early November 2026.
The 13.76 km underground section from Dairy Circle to Nagawara (12 stations) is
targeted for early 2027. The full line is 21.26 km with 18 stations. When it opens it
will interchange with the Yellow Line at Jayadeva Hospital and with the Purple Line at
MG Road, and will give Bannerghatta Road, JP Nagar, Shivajinagar and Nagawara a direct
north-south metro spine. Until then, no journey should be planned on it.

## Metro fares and ticketing
Metro fares range from Rs 10 for a short hop to Rs 90 for the longest journey across
the network, in Rs 10 steps. In the BMRCL feed the fare between any two stations is

SOURCE FILE: curated/policy_docs/06_metro_and_multimodal.md

determined entirely by how many stations the journey spans: 1-2 stops Rs 10, 3-4 Rs 20,
5-6 Rs 30, 7-8 Rs 40, 9-10 Rs 50, 11-15 Rs 60, 16-20 Rs 70, 21-25 Rs 80, and 26 or more
stops Rs 90. Tickets are bought as tokens, on a travel card, or through the Namma Metro
app with a QR ticket. A 5 per cent fare revision announced for 9 February 2026 was kept
in abeyance and has not been implemented, so the Rs 10-90 table remains in force.

There is no student monthly pass among BMRCL's published fare products. The state
free student pass scheme covers the four road transport corporations, not the metro,
so the metro leg of a student commute is always paid. A student who travels Silk
Institute to Majestic pays the metro fare for that leg even if the bus legs on
either side are free.

## Timings
Metro services typically start around 05:00 and run until about 23:00, with
slightly later services on weekends. The GTFS feed carries per-trip timings, but
BMRCL does not publish per-stop times for intermediate stations; the feed's
intermediate times are estimated from stop spacing and average speed and can be a
couple of minutes out.

## Combining bus and metro
The useful pattern for a long commute is: feeder bus or short BMTC ride to the
nearest metro station, metro across the city, then a bus from the metro station
nearest the destination. For the Harohalli corridor the practical version is:

1. BMTC or KSRTC ordinary bus from the student's locality to Silk Institute metro
   station, which sits at 12.8616 N, 77.5299 E.
2. Green Line north to Majestic if the destination is central.

SOURCE FILE: curated/policy_docs/06_metro_and_multimodal.md

3. A BMTC bus from Majestic to the final destination.

This only beats a single-seat bus when the destination is near a metro line and the
bus route is congested. For a DSU Harohalli student whose home is on the Kanakapura
Road side, route 213-V straight through is usually simpler than bus-metro-bus, and
it is free under the student pass.

## Metro access details
BMRCL's GTFS includes station entrances, pathways and platform levels. Stations with
multiple entrances can save a lot of walking if you pick the right one: for example,
Majestic has separate entrances for the Green and Purple platforms. The pathway data
carries traversal times, which matter when making a tight interchange.

## Auto and last-mile
Autos are outside the scope of this dataset. Auto fares in Bengaluru were last
revised separately from bus fares and are metered. For a short last-mile hop from a
metro station, walking to the nearest bus stop is usually cheaper than an auto, and
the free student pass covers the bus.

## Smart card and NCMC discounts on Namma Metro
Smart card and NCMC fares are discounted from the token fare:
- Monday to Saturday: 5% during peak hours and 10% during non-peak hours.
- Sundays and national holidays (26 January, 15 August, 2 October): 10% throughout the business day.
- Non-peak hours run from the start of revenue hours to 08:00, from 12:00 to 16:00, and from 21:00 to the end of revenue hours. All other times are peak.

## Namma Metro helpdesk and contact

SOURCE FILE: curated/policy_docs/07_bmrcl_official_fares.md

CONTACT NAMMA METRO HELP-DESK 1800-425-12345 FOR MORE DETAILS.

## Children below 3 feet travel free
Tickets are not required for children below 3 feet. No age criteria is considered.

## Penalty for ticketless travel or a lost ticket
Penalty for ticketless travel or lost ticket is Rs.200/- apart from maximum token fare.

## Penalty for mismatch (skipped entry or exit)
Skipping of any entry or exit is termed as MISMATCH. The penalty for mismatch is Rs10.Minimum Fare will be charged for entering into a station.

## Token validity and revalidation
Entry through the Automatic Gate must be made within 30 minutes of purchasing a token. After 30 minutes, an administrative charge of Rs. 5/- applies for revalidation.

## Overstay rule and penalty
A passenger holding a valid ticket can exit from paid area of same station within 20 minutes and from paid area of other stations within 120 minutes. For overstaying in paid area beyond these limits, penalty of Rs 50 per hour is charged subject to a maximum of Rs 100.

## Luggage allowance
One Luggage, with a maximum dimension of 60 cm x 45 cm x 25 cm (length x breadth x height) is allowed per person. To allow commuters to carry extra luggage/ additional baggage and oversized baggages, charges at the rate of Rs. 30/- per baggage is levied. This luggage ticket can be purchased from Customer Care Center(CCC).

## Penalty for unpaid luggage

SOURCE FILE: curated/policy_docs/07_bmrcl_official_fares.md

If ticket is not purchased for the additional baggage, then a penalty of Rs.250/- will be imposed. In case of any dispute, notwithstanding that commuter holds a valid ticket for travel, will be liable to be removed from the train by any metro railway officials authorised by the metro railway administration in this behalf or by any other person whom such metro railway official may call to his aid.

## Smart card validity extension
Add-value in the Smart Card shall be valid for ten years from the date of last add-value. The validity extension can be done by paying administrative charges of Rs. 20/- at Customer Care Center of any station.

## How many tokens one passenger may buy
The maximum number of tokens which are to be issued by the Ticket office operator to a single passenger at a time is six.

## Token removed from the exit gate
If the commuter takes away the token from the exit door without paying the deposit of Rs. 200.00 is penalized.

## How to top up a smart card
Stored Value can be added to Smart Card at any BMRCL Ticket counters or through online mode.through Namma Metro App(official) , BMRCL website or PayTM App, or Amazon Pay App).

## Smart card discount over the token fare
Get 5% discount for smart card, over token fare.

## Minimum top-up and cost of a new smart card
The top-up in case of Stored Value ticket shall be minimum Rs50 and further in multiples of Rs50. The cost of contactless smart card is Rs50 which is different from the stored value.

## Maximum stored value on a smart card

SOURCE FILE: curated/policy_docs/07_bmrcl_official_fares.md

Total maximum stored value on a smart card is Rs 3000/-. when top-up done at BMRCL metro stations. However, when top up is done at other outlets i.e. through BMRCL website or Namma Metro App or PayTM or Amazon Pay the amount is restricted to Rs 2950/-

## Group booking discount (100 to 1000 people)
A discount of 20% over the token fare, where the commuters enter a station all together and exit from a common destination station all together

## Group booking discount (more than 1000 people)
A discount of 25% over the token fare, where the commuters enter a station all together and exit from a common destination station all together.
